item.content:encoded:
多频道新闻雷达 — 军事新闻

2026-07-13 · 窗口: 24h · 条目: 54 · 生成时间: 2026-07-13 04:45 UTC

板块速览

过去24小时全球军事格局出现剧烈震荡：美伊围绕霍尔木兹海峡的攻防战骤然升级，成为国际安全最突出的火药桶；乌克兰战场则出现打击俄方油轮的新战法，试图切断克里米亚陆桥；南海仲裁案十周年之际，14国联合声明引发中方强烈反弹，南海地缘博弈再起波澜。以下为关键动态简报。

  • 伊朗对海湾国家发动攻击，美国实施数月来最重空袭：华盛顿邮报报道，伊朗针对海湾国家发射导弹，美军随即对伊朗防空与导弹设施进行多轮打击，双方已进入“攻击-报复”循环。
  • 美伊争夺霍尔木兹海峡控制权，全球能源动脉面临直接威胁：雅虎新闻指出，双方在海峡附近的攻击已直接威胁全球约20%石油运输通道，航运保险费率飙升。
  • 乌克兰宣称在亚速海击中大量俄方船舶，试图切断克里米亚陆桥：俄方证实一艘油轮遭袭，基辅邮报分析此举意在切断俄军通往克里米亚的陆地补给线。
  • 南海仲裁案裁决十周年，美日等14国发表联合声明施压中国：DW和共同社报道，14国声明指责中国南海“扩张”，中国外交部强硬回应称日本无资格置喙。
  • 解放军J-16战斗机罕见展示“野兽模式”携弹量，引发关注：印度时报分析认为该配置可能用于对地/对海饱和攻击，旨在威慑潜在对手。
  • 美国空军LRASM和JASSM产量将翻三倍，合同总额剧增：海军新闻披露，美空军计划未来五年采购超1.1万枚远程反舰导弹和联合空面防区外导弹，针对大国竞争储备弹药。

后续观察：霍尔木兹海峡冲突若持续升级，可能引发更大规模军事对峙甚至断航，油价和全球供应链将遭受冲击。乌克兰针对俄油轮的攻击显示战争正向海上能源基础设施延伸。南海方向，14国声明虽无强制执行效力，但将进一步固化区域安全阵营化；中国海军近期密集展示远程打击与水下战略武器能力，是对外部压力的直接回应。美欧同时在大西洋和印太加大导弹采购与反高超音速研发投入，表明军备竞赛正从概念走向量产。

国际安全 · 24 条

概览：美伊在霍尔木兹海峡的军事互殴成为国际安全头号焦点，双方已完成多轮打击，美国中央司令部称最新波次瞄准伊朗防空与导弹能力。同时，中国J-16战机挂载能力引发技术关注，台湾方面成立新反舰导弹单位也值得留意。

  • 伊朗向海湾国家发起攻击，美军发动数月来最大规模空袭 —— 伊朗攻击海湾国家为回击美方制裁与军事施压，战火已从波斯湾蔓延至阿拉伯半岛。
  • 美伊为霍尔木兹海峡控制权交手，全球能源动脉告急 —— 雅虎与WSJ均指出海峡通行量虽较5月有所回升（从233次增至576次），但仍远低于去年同期的3131次，航运保险与绕行成本高企。
  • 台湾海军组建配备美制鱼叉导弹的海岸打击指挥部 —— 军事观察杂志分析，此举意在强化反舰能力，应对解放军可能的两栖攻击。

收束判断：美伊冲突有演变为长期消耗战的趋势，霍尔木兹海峡的“常态化”高风险将对全球能源市场产生持续冲击，各国海军在波斯湾的护航与对峙压力剧增。

概览：乌克兰与俄罗斯在亚速海的海上冲突出现新形态，乌克兰声称以远程无人机击中多艘俄方油轮，意在打击俄能源经济并切断克里米亚补给线。中东战局则分流了西方对乌克兰的关注，欧盟外长会议与北约峰会均需同时处理两场冲突。

  • 乌克兰宣称在亚速海击中“一大批”俄方船舶 —— 战争地带报道，此次攻击主要针对运输燃料的油轮，俄国内能源价格与战争供应已受影响。与此印证的是俄方证实油轮被击中。
  • 中东冲突正转移西方对乌克兰的注意力 —— 俄军事媒体和RTÉ均指出，欧盟外长会议和土耳其内阁讨论中，乌克兰议题被中东危机挤占。
  • 乌克兰前线地区逼近IPC第3级粮食安全危机 —— ReliefWeb发布的预报显示，靠近前线的地区在2027年1月前将持续处于危机状态。

收束判断：乌克兰在海上的不对称打击取得一定效果，但无法根本改变地面战线；西方战略资源被迫两线分散，乌克兰军援面临不确定性。粮食危机则成为冲突的长期次生灾害。

  • 日美等14国就南海仲裁案裁决发表联合声明 —— 共同社报道，声明正值7月12日裁决十周年，呼吁中国停止“军事化”和“胁迫性行为”。
  • 中国驻欧盟使团和外交部严词回应：日本无资格说三道四，中国不信邪 —— 香港电台报道，中方谴责声明破坏地区稳定。环球时报社评称“14国声明想恐吓谁？中国人民不信邪也不怕邪”。
  • 中国海军水下发射战略导弹信息量巨大 —— 风闻评论称此次发射意在强化海基核威慑，回应外部军事压力。
  • 解放军J-16挂载“野兽模式”引印媒关注 —— 印度时报解读为针对航母和基地的饱和打击能力。

收束判断：南海仲裁案声明更多是政治姿态，但中国在军力展示上（重型挂载、水下导弹）做出实质回应，表明不会因外交压力而改变行动。未来南海摩擦可能因“灰色地带”行动增加而升高。

  • 美空军LRASM和JASSM产量将翻三倍，采购超1.1万枚 —— 海军新闻称，合同目标明确针对未来高强度冲突中的弹药消耗储备，尤其瞄准西太平洋与中东方向。
  • 欧盟签署HYDIS高超音速拦截器概念阶段拨款 —— MBDA主导的“天鹰座”拦截器完成最终概念评审，进入3年开发期，回应中俄高超音速武器威胁。
  • 德国海军计划2029年前列装MBDA与莱茵金属联合激光武器 —— 德国BAAINBw签署合同，预期用于近程反无人机及反舰导弹防御。
  • 霍尔木兹海峡6月通行量较5月翻倍仍远低于往年，冲突风险持续 —— USNI新闻援引Lloyd's List Intelligence数据，6月576次通行对比5月233次，但同比下降82%。

News Radar — 军事新闻

2026-07-13 · Window: 24h · Items: 54 · Generated: 2026-07-13 04:45 UTC

Editor's Brief

The last 24 hours have seen a dramatic escalation in the U.S.-Iran standoff, with multiple rounds of strikes traded over the Strait of Hormuz, directly threatening global energy supplies. Concurrently, Ukraine has claimed a major drone strike on Russian ships in the Sea of Azov, while China and its neighbors marked the tenth anniversary of the South China Sea arbitration ruling with renewed rhetorical and military posturing. The Indo-Pacific naval landscape is also evolving, with new missile production surges and anti-drone systems entering development. The convergence of these flashpoints suggests a period of heightened, multi-theater volatility that defense planners must account for.

  • The U.S. and Iran have exchanged heavy strikes over the weekend, with CENTCOM completing a wave of attacks targeting Iranian air defenses and missile capabilities. Iran simultaneously launched attacks on Gulf states, and both sides vie for control of the Strait of Hormuz (WSJ, The Washington Post).
  • Ukraine claims its long-range drones struck scores of Russian ships in the Sea of Azov, targeting oil tankers and adding to Russia's energy woes (The War Zone). Russia confirmed a tanker was hit (The Moscow Times).
  • China's J-16 fighter displayed its heaviest-ever missile loadout in a 'Beast Mode' configuration, drawing regional attention (The Times of India).
  • Fourteen nations, including Japan and the U.S., issued a joint statement on the tenth anniversary of the South China Sea arbitration ruling, declaring China's maritime claims have no legal basis (RFI). China responded dismissively, calling the ruling a "farce" (新蓝网).
  • The U.S. Air Force plans to more than triple production of LRASM and JASSM cruise missiles, buying over 11,000 units in the next five to seven years (Naval News).
  • The EU has signed a grant for the MBDA-led HYDIS hypersonic interceptor project, aiming for a three-year concept phase for the AQUILA interceptor (Naval News).
  • Despite ongoing Iranian attacks, the number of transits through the Strait of Hormuz more than doubled from May to June 2026, though still far below year-ago levels (USNI News).

Watch next: The U.S.-Iran exchange appears far from de-escalation; further strikes on Iranian air defense and missile sites are likely, with potential knock-on effects on oil prices and Gulf state security. Ukraine's Sea of Azov campaign may force Russia to redeploy naval assets, while the South China Sea diplomatic row could trigger new military drills or incidents. Monitor the Strait of Hormuz traffic data and insurance rates for shipping.

国际安全 · 24 items

The past 24 hours have been dominated by a dramatic escalation between the United States and Iran over the Strait of Hormuz. Multiple waves of U.S. strikes targeted Iranian air defenses and missile capabilities, while Iran retaliated with attacks on Gulf states. The conflict has disrupted one of the world's most critical energy chokepoints, with transits still dramatically below normal. Meanwhile, Ukraine's claims of striking Russian ships in the Sea of Azov and China's J-16 'Beast Mode' display add to the global security landscape.

  • The U.S. and Iran traded new rounds of strikes, with CENTCOM completing a wave focusing on Iranian air defenses and missiles (The Jerusalem Post). Iran launched attacks on Gulf states as U.S. strikes escalated (The Washington Post).
  • The Strait of Hormuz remains the epicenter, with both sides vying for control. Attacks have targeted the waterway critical to global energy supplies (Yahoo).
  • Ukraine claims it struck scores of Russian ships in the Sea of Azov, targeting oil tankers (The War Zone), adding a new dimension to the conflict.
  • China's J-16 fighter showcased a 'Beast Mode' loadout, highlighting its growing strike capabilities (The Times of India).
  • A separate article noted the US Air Force is set for a $240 million upgrade as Trump leaves office (Simple Flying).

Signal: The U.S.-Iran standoff shows no sign of de-escalation; further strikes on both sides are expected to continue, with potential for broader regional involvement.

冲突局势 · 12 items

The conflict landscape is marked by the ongoing U.S.-Iran escalation drawing Western attention away from Ukraine, while Russia's war in Ukraine continues to see new strikes on its maritime assets. Food security in Ukraine is deteriorating near frontlines, and diplomatic efforts (EU, NATO, Turkey) are trying to manage both theatres. A rare humanitarian note comes from the Pope urging dialogue.

  • The Middle East conflict is diverting Western focus and resources from Ukraine, as noted by Russian military analysis (Военное дело). This could create an opportunity for Russian advances.
  • Ukraine claims to have struck scores of Russian ships in the Sea of Azov, with Russia confirming a tanker was hit (The Moscow Times). This signals Ukraine's growing ability to strike Russian economic assets.
  • Ukraine's food security outlook warns of Crisis (IPC Phase 3) outcomes in frontline areas from June 2026 to January 2027 (ReliefWeb).
  • Pope Francis called for the winds of war not to extinguish hope and for a return to dialogue (Vatican News).
  • EU foreign ministers and Turkey's cabinet are separately scheduled to discuss Ukraine, NATO, and Middle East crises (RTE.ie, Report.az).

Signal: The risk of a two-front crisis is real; if the U.S.-Iran conflict deepens, Ukraine could face reduced support, potentially altering the battlefield balance.

中国军情 · 10 items

China's military posture in the South China Sea and its growing air power dominated this desk. The tenth anniversary of the 2016 South China Sea arbitration ruling saw 14 nations, led by Japan and the U.S., issue a joint statement declaring China's claims legally baseless. China dismissed the statement as a 'farce' and accused Japan of having no standing. Meanwhile, a Chinese submarine-launched ballistic missile test was flagged as a significant signal, and the J-16 'Beast Mode' display reinforced Beijing's conventional deterrence.

  • Japan, the U.S., and 12 other nations issued a joint statement on the anniversary of the South China Sea arbitration ruling, stating China's expansion has no legal basis (RFI). China fired back, calling the move an attempt to intimidate (新浪财经).
  • A Chinese article described the submarine-launched strategic missile test as 'explosive' in its implications, signaling Beijing's undersea nuclear deterrence (风闻).
  • The J-16 fighter's heaviest-ever missile loadout (dubbed 'Beast Mode') was highlighted by Indian media, noting its potential for air-to-ground strikes (The Times of India).
  • China's foreign ministry separately rebuked Japan for commenting on South China Sea sovereignty, reiterating its firm stance (香港電台).
  • The Republic of China (Taiwan) Navy formed a new coastal combat command armed with U.S. Harpoon missiles, marking a shift in its defensive posture (Military Watch Magazine).

Signal: The South China Sea diplomatic war is intensifying; expect China to conduct military exercises in response to the 14-nation statement, potentially increasing risk of incidents with regional navies.

海军与印太 · 8 items

Naval and Indo-Pacific developments cover three main threads: the ongoing Strait of Hormuz crisis and its impact on shipping, major arms production increases (U.S. LRASM/JASSM, EU hypersonic interceptor), and force modernization (German Navy laser weapon, anti-drone warfare, RIMPAC exercises). The U.S. Navy also issued a new medical shaving waiver policy, while a Congressional report details extended nuclear deterrence.

  • Despite Iranian attacks, Strait of Hormuz transits doubled from May to June 2026 (to 576), but remain a fraction of pre-crisis levels (3,131 in June 2025) (USNI News). The shipping industry is adjusting to high-risk operations.
  • The U.S. Air Force plans to triple LRASM and JASSM production, with a planned procurement of over 11,000 missiles over five to seven years (Naval News). This dramatically expands the Pentagon's inventory for long-range anti-ship and strike capabilities.
  • The EU signed a grant for the MBDA-led HYDIS hypersonic interceptor project, launching a three-year concept phase for the AQUILA interceptor (Naval News). This addresses the growing hypersonic threat.
  • The German Navy selected MBDA and Rheinmetall to develop a high-energy laser weapon, with deployment expected by 2029 (Naval News). This marks a step toward directed-energy naval air defense.
  • A report on anti-drone warfare at sea emphasizes the need for AESA radar and hard-kill effectors to counter Tier 2 drone threats (Naval News).
  • RIMPAC 2026 is now in its at-sea phase, with live-firing drills including Canadian frigates (USNI News).
  • A Congressional Research Service report on U.S. extended deterrence and regional nuclear capabilities was released, highlighting assurance to over 30 allies (USNI News).

Signal: The U.S. is massively investing in long-range standoff missiles, while European navies focus on hypersonic and laser defenses—indicating a shift away from short-range systems toward distributed, longer-range engagements in a contested maritime environment.
